## PR #141: after-deploy cost reading

Deployment: **PID 7956**, source build **acf3646c035ac4816ff56cbf29ea58ff238c6d5b**, per pm-001's merge/bounce record. Main was independently at that revision and the installed executable pointed to its release target. Both ping snapshots reported PID 7956, healthy, build label `pij-rs 0.1.0`; that label does not embed a Git SHA. Independent process snapshots confirmed the same PID, executable and start time, **2026-11-07 18:49:27 +10:00**, throughout.

| Metric | AFTER |
|---|---|
| Daemon launches | **171 to 225: +54 / 60.001757 s = 0.899974/s** |
| Machine-wide launches | **153.2/s**, niced 20.0 s sample |
| Daemon CPU | **8.62 CPU seconds / 60.001757 s = 14.37%** of one CPU over the interval |
| Daemon RSS | **134,096 to 137,104 KiB = 130.95 to 133.89 MiB** |
| Load averages | Start **24.95 / 31.08 / 35.34**, end **34.14 / 32.28 / 35.47** |

Ping window: **2026-11-07 18:50:41.261012 to 18:51:41.262917 +10:00** (08:50:41.261012 to 08:51:41.262917 UTC). Elapsed time is monotonic between snapshot starts. Endpoint `ps` CPU percentages were **3.1% and 17.7%**; these rolling values are not the cumulative-CPU interval calculation above.

### All daemon counter deltas

| Operation | Delta |
|---|---:|
| `ddocs.community` | 0 |
| `gh.delivered` | 0 |
| `git.community` | 0 |
| `git.pa-watchdog-common-dir` | 0 |
| `ps.registration-native-process` | 0 |
| `ps.sidecar-process-group` | 0 |
| `ps.uds-peer-start` | **54** |
| `tmux.control-client` | 0 |
| `tmux.pipe-pane attach` | 0 |
| `tmux.set-options tap owner` | 0 |
| **Total** | **54** |

The per-operation deltas sum to the total. No counter decreased and the PID/start time remained unchanged. Every incremental daemon launch was recorded at the existing peer-authentication site, not a new directory-view launch site. This does not isolate the view's CPU, SQL or file-reading cost.

### Machine-wide coverage and comparison

Ran `nice -n 19 just spawn-rate --seconds 20 --json` from deployed main, in parallel with the daemon window. The unchanged probe independently identified listening PID 7956. It made **246,620 in-process libproc polls** over 20 s: the niced probe is itself a busy-polling CPU observer, so machine CPU/load is not unperturbed.

Parent-attribution lower bounds were **96.2/s gone before inspection**, **55.2/s other**, and **0.5/s direct daemon children**. That 20 s lower bound cannot be equated to the 60 s daemon counter rate. Observed command lower bounds included bash **28.4/s**, node **9.4/s**, copilot **1.1/s**, and cargo **0.1/s**.

The plan 203 historical BEFORE in `docs/plans/203-prime-prompts/assets/evidence/phase-1.md` was about **0.7 daemon launches/s** and **157.8 machine-wide** during concurrent builds. This AFTER is **0.900/s** and **153.2/s**, but the differing workloads and windows prevent causal comparison.

For another recent reference, #144's deployment note recorded PID 50992 on build e6958e7: **0.716583 daemon launches/s**, **146.8 machine-wide**, **16.70% daemon interval CPU**, and **142.73 to 143.91 MiB RSS** at 17:43-17:44. It was an active-fleet observation too, not a matched #141 BEFORE. Counters were never subtracted across daemon incarnations.

**The requested AFTER reading is complete, but not a controlled idle regression test.** Load remained high and active shell/Node/build traffic was observed. No claim that #141 caused a machine-wide rate change, or that its view's instance grouping is now measured. P141-N001's high-instance-cardinality CPU/memory qualification remains.

Raw counter/process/load readings and the machine probe report are retained as session evidence (`pr141-after-window.json`, `pr141-after-machine.json`). No builds, tests, stress traffic, source edits or daemon restart were performed.
